lawyer:
Sheikh Md. Sobel, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
Ashique Rubaiat, with Rakibul Alam, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 2. 
Kh. Bahar Rumy (KB Runny), DAG with Salma Sultana, DAG and Md. Habibur Rahman Sarker, AAG and Emdad Shahnewaj Chwodhury, AAG and Monjur Elahi Porag, AAG—For the Respondent No.1.
parties:
Masud Ahmed (Tagar) -------- Petitioner
Vs.
Artha Rin Adalat, Jashore and another --------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Akram Hossain Chowdhury, J: At the instance of the defendant-petitioner, upon an application under Article 102 (1) & (2)(a) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the Rule Nisi was issued in the following term:-"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the assumption of jurisdiction by the respondent No. 1 to try Miscellaneous Case No. 87 of 1990 for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 19-8-1990 passed by the Civil Court, Viz, Subordinate Judge, Jessore in Money Suit No. 20 of 1987 shall not be declared to be made without lawful authority and of no legal effect; and why a direction for the trial of the same as proceeding in the ordinary Court and not as a proceeding under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain shall not be made and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 2. At the time of issuance of the Rule on 16-3-2002, by the ad-interim order, all further proceedings of Miscellaneous Case No. 87 of 1990 was stayed till hearing of the Rule. 

 4. The petitioner who was- shown as defendant No. 2 while came to know about the said ex-parte decree, he then and then filed an application under Order IX, rulel3 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (Shortly CPC) in the then Sub-ordinate Judge, Jessore on 26-8-1990 praying for restoring the suit to its original file and number upon setting aside the aforesaid ex-parte decree dated 19-8-1990 which has been thus registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 87 of 1990. 

 5. During pendency of the said Miscellaneous Case, since the Arthorin Adalat Ain, 1990 has been enacted, the case record was then withdrawn and transferred, automatically from the Court of Subordinate Judge to the Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore but that process was actually held beyond the knowledge of the defendant-petitioner. The Artha Rin Adalat upon then receiving the case record on 20-11-1990 and on the said very day passed an order, in absence of the parties, directing the petitioner to deposit some of Taka 3,41,875 (three lacs forty one thousand eight hundred seventy five) in favour of the plaintiff bank within 26-12-1990. The said order was never communicated to the petitioner and that he has also got no opportunity to comply the said direction, as well. It further asserted in the writ petition that on 5-1-1991 the petitioner for the first time came to learn about the above facts and order of direction as stated above and he on the said very day filed an application for exemption from making the deposit as directed above. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore however, on the said very day" i.e. on 5-1-2991 has rejected the said prayer of the defendant petitioner and also rejected the application for restoration of the suit in its file and number, as well. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the said rejection order the petitioner was constrained to prefer FMA No. 44 of 1991 before this Court along with an application for staying all further proceeding of Money Execution Case No. 10 of 1991. Eventually, a Division Bench of this Court upon hearing the said FMA No. 44 of 1991 vide judgment and order dated 13-4-1994 had been pleased to allow the same by setting aside the order impugned in the said appeal dated 5-1-1991 and sent back the Miscellaneous Case to the Court below for its disposal. Then during pendency of the said Miscellaneous Case before the respondent No. 1 i.e. the Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore, the petitioner filed an application on 3-5-2000 praying that since the Artha Rin Adalat has no jurisdiction to hear the Miscellaneous case, because the matter do not arisen from recovery of loan and therefore prayed for transfer the Miscellaneous Case No. 87 of 1990 to the 1st Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Jessore where it was earlier. However, the respondent No. 1, the Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore vide order dated 21-1-2001 was pleased to reject the same, summarily. 

 7. The petitioner feeling aggrieved by the said .rejection order being finding no other alternative efficacious remedy, hence moved this Court by filing the present writ petition and obtained the Rule along with an ad-interim order of stay, as above, staying all further proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No. 87 of 1990 as was pending in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore, till hearing of the Rule. 

 8. Mr. Sheikh Md. Sohel, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that since the Miscellaneous Case No. 87 of 1990 was arose from the Money Suit filed for realization of money defalcated by the then Manager of the Bank which does not at all come within the mischief of the definition of loan as defined under section 2 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. Learned Advocate to that extent referring to sub-section (Kha) of section 2 of the said Ain shown us the definition of loan and then submits that which actually relates with recovery of Bank's loan as disbursed assuring repayment and to be tried, in case of, failing repayment of said loan as under the Artho Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. But the present case was being initiated for realization of defalcated money which does not, any way, comes within the purview of "GL" as defined under the law, as stated above. Learned Advocate next submits that if so, ignoring those clear legal provision, the Miscellaneous case is continued and then disposed of in the Artha Rin Adalat, it will be a wrong decision treating the same to be held in Coranz non-judice which will be thus violated the petitioner's fundamental right as guaranteed under Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution of the. People's of Bangladesh. Learned Advocate therefore urges for making the Rule absolute directing the Artha Rin Adalat, Jashore to send the case back to the original Court where it was earlier about to decide the Miscellaneous case No. 87 of 1990 as filed under Order IX, rule 13 of the CPC and dispose of the same by the said competent Court who has the proper jurisdiction. 

 9. In opposing the Rule, Mr. Ashique Rubaiat appearing with Mr. Rakibul Alam, learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2, Sonali Bank who by filing affidavit-in-opposition emphasis to his submission that the definition as Cescribed in Sub-section (Kha) of Section 02 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 clearly states that the loan "ঋণ” means “অন্য যে কোনো আর্থিক আনুকল্য বা সুযোগ, যে নামেই অভিযুক্ত হোক না কেন” He then referring to Sub-section 4 of section 5 pointed out before us that the jurisdiction of the Artha Rin Adalat defined therein as of a civil Court. To that extent, he argues that since the Artho Rin Adalat has the jurisdiction and power to try in all matters like the present one, the Miscellaneous case was thus correctly transferred there, in the Artha Rin Adalat. Learned Advocate therefore urges for discharging the Rule. 

 10. In reply to the above submissions as placed by the learned Advocate for the respondent No.2, the learned Advocate for the petitioner Mr Sheikh Md. Sohel again referring to the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 submits that the Act, 1990 itself made difference between loan money and the Money defalcated and to that extent, it has been decided by this Court in the case of Agrani Bank, Janna Branch, Manikgonj vs AFM Emdadul Haq, reported in 50 DLR 173 and in the case of Eastern Bank Limited vs Subordiante Judge and another, reported in 49 DLR 531 that the suit since has been filed not for realization of any loan money from the defendant who was admittedly not a loanee but one of the defendant claiming to have misappropriated the bank money and, as such, by no stress of imagination the suit comes within the purview of Artha Rin Ain. By placing the above such decisions the learned Advocate for the petitioner vehemently opposes the respondent's argument as made herein above and thus he prays for making the Rule absolute. 

 11. However, Mr. Ashique Rubaiat, learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2, at the end frankly submits that if so, the Miscellaneous case proceeded in accordance with law and dispose of expeditiously, he has no objection but it to be disposed of within a certain period for the sake of early disposal of the suit about to make relief to the parties of the suit who are suffering from mental agony for long, since 1990. 

 12. Learned DAG however by adopting the submissions of respondent No. 2 above contended that since it is a long pending case, it should be disposed of expeditiously and in accordance with law. 

 13. We have heard the learned Advocates above and perused the materials on record and to appreciate the submissions of the learned Advocates, we have given our anxious consideration to their submissions placed and thus we have gone through the documents submitted with the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and the reference placed as well as the law relates in the matter in hand, in particular. Upon going through the record, we finds that the original suit was not filed for realization of any loan but admittedly filed for realization of an amount of money defalcated by the Manager of the Bank where the present-petitioner was shown as defendant No. 2 alleging that he was the beneficiary of getting the money above but other than nothing averment was made against him. Even then, since an ex-parte decree was passed in his absence, he was compelled to file the Miscellaneous Case under Order 9, rule 13 of the CPC who has thus sought to give him a chance to place his pleadings in the Miscellaneous case. However, without giving any notice of transferring or hearing the said Miscellaneous case, the same was automatically transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore and not only that has also been disposed of therein, in absence of the petitioner, on the reason that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 has been enacted in the meantime. The materials on record even as so, reveals that the suit was started and proceeded initially in a normal Civil Court by filing a Money Suit and since an ex-parte decree was passed in the said Money Suit, the Miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the CPC was filed for setting aside the ex-parte decree. Upon perusal of the law itself as well as going through the decisions placed, as those made by this Court, in this regard, in 50 DLR 173 and 49 DLR 531, we are thus at one with the said decisions holding that the Miscellaneous Case being arose from a money suit which was filed for realization of allegedly misappropriated money but not for recovery of loan money, it should be heard and disposed of by the regular Civil Court but not by the Artha Rain Adalat. Thus, we are of the opinion that the Money suit as was being filed not for realization of loan money but for realizing the misappropriated money as alleged, the Miscellaneous Case should be decided by the normal Civil Court where it was earlier. Having regarded so, we are inclined to dispose of the Rule directing the parties to agitate their pleadings and grievances in the Court where the Miscellaneous case was earlier but not in the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 14. In the premises above, the Rule is disposed of without however any order as to cost. The order of stay as granted earlier, at the time of issuance of the Rule, is hereby recalled and vacated. The Miscellaneous Case No. 87 of 1990 is to be tried by the then Sub-ordinate Judge and now the Joint District Judge, Jashore. The said learned Judge however, is directed to dispose of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case expeditiously, preferably within 4 (four) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order, however upon giving proper notice to the contending parties to the suit/case.
